subject: pharmacology
title: Contraceptives, emergency cover and uterotonics

steps.tx: **Combined oral contraceptives** block ovulation, thicken cervical mucus and thin the endometrium through ethinyl estradiol with a progestin component. Absolute contraindications include **venous thromboembolism**, migraine with aura, smoking after thirty five years, uncontrolled hypertension and breast cancer because arterial and venous clots increase. Benefits include lower ovarian and endometrial cancer, better acne and dysmenorrhoea and less anaemia, while **rifampicin** and enzyme inducers cause contraceptive failure.
steps.say: Combined pills prevent ovulation and thicken cervical mucus against sperm penetration. Migraine with aura, smoking after thirty five and previous clots forbid combined pills. Enzyme inducers such as rifampicin cause contraceptive failure without backup protection. Benefits are clear and include less dysmenorrhoea, better acne and a reduced ovarian cancer risk.

steps.tx: The paired groin ultrasounds show a femoral vein filled with echogenic **thrombus** beside the round femoral artery in the groin. With transducer compression the vein stays open and noncompressible, which confirms acute **deep vein thrombosis** rather than a normal collapsible vein. This complication explains why clinicians screen for clot risk, migraine aura and smoking before prescribing **combined oral contraceptives** to any patient.
steps.say: The ultrasound compares a thrombosed femoral vein before and during compression manoeuvres. A normal vein collapses fully while the thrombosed vein remains open and filled. Noncompressibility confirms deep vein thrombosis at the bedside without delay. This risk explains careful screening before combined contraceptive prescription.

steps.tx: **Missed pill rules** protect efficacy when patients take one late pill immediately and use seven days of backup after missing two or more pills. Combined pills start after six weeks postpartum during breastfeeding, while progestin only methods start earlier without delaying protection. **Transdermal patches and vaginal rings** bypass the gut but carry the same clot cautions, and malabsorption or interacting drugs should redirect patients toward **long acting reversible contraception**.
steps.say: Patients take a single late pill immediately and continue the pack normally. Missing two pills requires seven days of backup contraception for protection. Emergency contraception helps after unprotected intercourse during the pill free gap. Long acting methods bypass vomiting, malabsorption and interacting medicines reliably.

steps.tx: **Progestin only methods** suit breastfeeding patients, smokers and those with clot risk because they avoid oestrogen related thrombosis completely. The minipill needs a strict three hour window, **DMPA** injections last three months but cause weight gain, bone loss and delayed fertility return, and the **implant** provides three years of cover. The levonorgestrel intrauterine system treats menorrhagia, while the copper device provides hormone free protection for ten years.
steps.say: Progestin only methods suit patients who face clot risk or smoke regularly. The minipill requires dosing within a strict three hour window daily. Depot injections cause weight gain and reversible bone loss over time. Implants and intrauterine devices provide years of highly effective contraception.

vis.alt: A table comparing progestin-only pill, DMPA, implant, Mirena IUS, and copper IUD, detailing duration, side effects, and suitability.
vis.caption: Key features of progestin-only and copper LARC methods

steps.tx: **Emergency contraception** works best with a copper intrauterine device within five days, which also provides ongoing contraception for years afterwards. **Levonorgestrel** works within seventy two hours and ulipristal within one hundred and twenty hours, although interacting drugs reduce oral efficacy. Medical abortion combines **mifepristone** with misoprostol, and postpartum haemorrhage needs oxytocin, tranexamic acid within three hours, massage and transfusion support.
steps.say: The copper device provides the most effective emergency contraception within five days. Levonorgestrel works within seventy two hours while ulipristal extends cover to five days. Mifepristone blocks progesterone and misoprostol expels the pregnancy afterwards. Postpartum haemorrhage requires oxytocin, tranexamic acid and uterine massage urgently.
